- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–8% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5-day average is rising and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, expect slight lag — delay peak by 1–2 days.  
- If forecast spikes after a sharp drop in sentiment, reduce the spike magnitude by 10–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2) over 3–5 days, model should not overcorrect — forecast should trend slightly lower, not sharply down.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast, adjust next forecast by adding 2–5% to the previous forecast’s last 3 days average.
